Database indexing accelerates data retrieval by creating data structures optimized for lookup. The most common index type is the B-tree, which provides logarithmic search, insert, and delete operations. Hash indexes offer O(1) lookup for equality queries. Inverted indexes map terms to document positions, enabling full-text search. Vector indexes like IVF and HNSW enable similarity search over embeddings. Modern databases often support multiple index types simultaneously, allowing query planners to choose the most efficient access path based on the query pattern and predicate selectivity.
